properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: SHA-1/SHA-2 library in the JS deploy tooling's node_modules. No first-party JS/TS source exists in this repo, so this is shipped-capability inventory, not a call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA signing in the EVM ecosystem: the ethers/ethereumjs-util tooling signs deployment transactions over this curve. First-party Solidity ECDSA verification (Crypto2FAHook) exists too and is reported as a separate finding. Replacement (ML-DSA) requires an ecosystem-wide change, not just this repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: OpenSSL-compatible single-round MD5 KDF in the tooling's node_modules. No first-party use anywhere in this repo (no JS/TS source); flagged as a weak-by-practice KDF that ships with the toolchain regardless.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Tooling-level ECDSA over secp256k1 (ethers signs deploy transactions with it). No first-party JS call site in this repo; the first-party Solidity ECDSA uses are reported separately as findings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dev tooling (ethers v5 + keccak for ethereumjs-util@7.1.5). On-chain counterpart — Solidity keccak256 — is used throughout the first-party contracts (EIP-712 digests, signature hash packing, CREATE2). Changeable only insofar as Ethereum's protocol hash is fixed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Pulled by ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 (line 1275) and ethers v5 (@ethersproject/pbkdf2 backs JSON-v3 keystore encryption). PBKDF2 iteration parameters are not visible in the lockfile. Dev-only tooling.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Availability asset: scrypt-js (the scrypt KDF ethers v5 uses to decrypt JSON keystores) ships in the tooling's node_modules. No first-party JS/TS source in this repo calls it; the first-party Solidity tree has no scrypt use at all.
